acceptance_status: Automated-inventory checkpoint; full functional/native/manual/performance/release parity remains open.
scope: Download panel text, progress and actions on one shared Rust/Metal scene, Rust panel allocation, native theme/font/event/focus/AX/scroll adapters and explicit widget/delegate ownership. Chromium download facts, formatted status, ordering, security checks and commands remain native.

build_input_snapshot.gn_delta: No target/dependency change. Rust bridge adds clear_selection for existing SelectState. Explicit native adapters, preference selector allocation/refresh and browser tests changed. Concurrent root network-policy work remains excluded.
build_input_snapshot.method: Frozen UI overlay base a3afc206f742f0a59da6e65d609ddf1df3c7326d plus 16 explicit live UI overrides (including sidebar_metal.h/mm), with committed own installer/stager hooks; concurrent network-policy changes excluded. Twenty-one prototype source hashes are matched to committed, live and staged inputs.

native_service_patch.license: Generated Chromium header and source hook retain the Chromium BSD-style license; project adapter/tool/model changes use Apache-2.0.

contracts: Download title/source/status/empty copy, progress and action controls contain no native Label, MdTextButton or ProgressBar in the opt-in backend. PanelScene reuses cached RenderText/native typography and Rust scenes with CPU fallback. All managed actions and progress join the same transparent panel underlay, without per-row drawable allocation. Views keeps its native controls.

Rust panel allocation replaces the outer panel, flex scroll viewport, list, row and horizontal action BoxLayouts. Native measurements, insets, spacing, scroll services and maximum-height policy remain inputs/adapters. A contents adapter forwards preferred-size changes so live text/control visibility updates refresh native scroll extent.

Rust kind26 renders determinate width with native pixel rounding, RTL reflection and flat default track geometry. Indeterminate segments use the original two-second native material keyframes. One panel timer runs only while a projected visible indeterminate node exists, stops for hidden/offscreen/nonanimated content and requests CPU fallback paint when Metal is absent. Native colors, 1x5 preferred metrics, progress AX names and percentage/indeterminate value semantics remain.

Common PanelScene now lives in the existing sidebar Metal interface; page dialogs retain the alias/factory and unchanged scene behavior. Shared action groups reuse Rust RowPointer input, native metric/font/color services and the existing kind19 recipe. The shared renderer collects these actions before treating other native interactive controls as cutouts; existing preference/tools/dialog underlay behavior remains covered.

Download widgets and plain delegates are now directly owned and synchronously released in widget-then-delegate order. The scene, row pointers and scroll subscriptions are cleared before widget destruction. Closing invalidates old UI callbacks and timers; profile changes still detach item/manager observers without cancelling transfers. Existing registered native accelerator routing now also serves the download window, including actual Cocoa Escape.

The real-transfer shared browser case compares label widths/heights, action preferred/minimum sizes and progress metrics/AX against original native controls, checks unknown progress and hide/show animation, then uses Cocoa Space to pause/resume and Escape to close. It also requires a resolved target path and verifies the full-path filename tooltip plus native tooltip-handler hit testing after layout. Review of the first passing rendering matrix found static-copy event targeting disabled that original tooltip; only filename copies now opt into native hit testing. A dedicated Metal case checks 80 real manager rows, no hidden native controls, first/last culling under actual scrolling, theme changes, CloseNow/reopen and profile-bound stale GUID rejection.

Actual Chromium DownloadItem/DownloadManager facts, byte/time status formatting, active-first/history-cap ordering, unsafe/missing/terminal transfer checks, observer scheduling and Act commands remain native and unchanged in authority. Rust scene presence never authorizes an action. Existing dangerous-history, transfer/Finder interception, cancellation and profile isolation cases remain in both gates.

No dependency or browser-service policy was added. Native View/Button/ScrollView/window/focus/AX nodes, download presentation/list policy and other service panels remain to migrate or accept as explicit platform adapters. No controlled CPU/GPU/drawable-presentation or memory improvement is established.

optional_scenarios.status: Not rerun for this presentation checkpoint. The earlier tools-chrome report retains four default-30-trial passes per backend; none is counted as a current-commit pass.

limits: Native titles/frames and modal/scroll/window/event/focus/AX containers, other forms/panels/layouts and remaining form construction/service wording remain open. Native browser validation, authority, stores and operations remain explicit adapters.
Manual IME/candidate-window, VoiceOver, global RTL, typography/scale/pixel fidelity, pointer/trackpad, detach/reattach and GPU recovery acceptance remain open.
No controlled CPU/GPU/drawable-presentation speedup or memory improvement is claimed.
Normal installed applications/profiles were untouched; no release bundle was packaged/signed. Final shipped-binary Apache-2.0/upstream license/notice acceptance remains open.
